title: I built a browser game with Claude Code, but I use ChatGPT to write the prompts. Does this actually make sense?
author: josemichus
selftext:
I've been building DRAIN RAGE, a retro shoot 'em up mixed with classic pinball mechanics, using Claude Code, Phaser and TypeScript. AI also helped me create the graphics and sound assets.

My workflow is a bit unusual: I discuss game mechanics and ideas with ChatGPT, ask it to prepare detailed implementation prompts, and then paste those prompts into Claude Code, which does the actual coding. I test the results, identify what doesn't feel right, and repeat the process.

The interesting part is that Claude can implement complex mechanics surprisingly well, but making them actually fun is a different story. Getting pinball-style collisions to feel natural or balancing weapons has taken many iterations.

I'm wondering whether using two AI models this way actually gives me an advantage, or if I'm just adding an unnecessary step. Maybe ChatGPT helps me think through the requirements before Claude starts coding?

Anyway, the first stage is playable now, and here's a short trailer!

Play it here: [https://josemichus.itch.io/drain-rage](https://josemichus.itch.io/drain-rage)

Does anyone else use ChatGPT to plan and prompt Claude Code, or do you handle everything directly in Claude?

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body:
Makes sense to me. Having one model turn your messy idea into a clear spec and the other just build it keeps Claude from guessing. Just watch the prompts don't get huge, short and specific per feature usually works better.

Also if you want, I run Vibe1Up, a free site that lists AI-made browser games. Happy to list yours there, just drop the link or DM me.
